title: auth cache propagation race causing customer 429 spikes and mitigation playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Executive summary: On 2026-02-14 we observed a multi-region spike of 429 responses affecting a subset of high-throughput customers. The immediate cause was incorrect accounting of active sessions after a token rotation flow introduced a window where the gateway and quota-enforcer had divergent views of token validity. This race caused duplicate accounting of requests for recently rotated tokens and triggered aggressive quota enforcement. Impact lasted ~90 minutes for affected customers before staged rollbacks and traffic shaping reduced errors. This ticket tracks root-cause analysis, permanent fixes, and observability / runbook improvements.

root_cause: A change to gateway auth caching TTL and a concurrent refactor in auth-service token rotation created a narrow window where a rotated token produced two valid-looking entries: the gateway cache marked the old token as invalidating but still allowed a short grace window, while quota-enforcer's shard-level cache still treated requests as coming from the pre-rotation identity. An off-by-one bug in token-version assignment during rotation caused some requests to be counted against both token versions for ~30-90s. This combined with a recent reduce in smoothing for quota enforcer to meet latency SLOs led to immediate hard rejections (429) rather than gradual backpressure.
impact: High for 12 customers in the 'alpha' and 'beta' tiers; median p50 latency unchanged, but 429 rate peaked at 18% for affected keys and caused timeouts in downstream apps. Revenue-impacting endpoints for 3 enterprise customers reported degraded functionality. No customer data exposure or other security issues identified.
